content.text: can you give me a bit more detail
can you give me a bit more detail

`FULL_SNAPSHOT` lets the importer treat an absent frame as a retirement candidate. That only works if the CSV represents **every frame in a declared scope at a specific point in time**.

Suppose our app has 100 active frames in a region. A CSV arrives with 97 rows. Those three absences could be legitimate removals, or the export could have stopped early. Both cases pass the current 10% retirement guard, so the guard alone can’t tell us which happened.

I’d require a **manifest from the export producer** with four fields:

| Field | What it tells us |
|---|---|
| Scope | Which country, region, or environment the export covers |
| Capture time | When the source inventory was read, so later edits can be protected |
| Expected row count | How many records the producer expected from a complete read of that scope |
| CSV checksum | Whether the uploaded bytes match the file the producer generated |

The important distinction is where the count comes from. If the producer counts the 97 lines after a partial export, the count and checksum can both pass. The producer needs to establish completeness from the source inventory, then bind that claim to the file it generated.

Once that check passes, the importer can evaluate the three missing frames. A frame edited or moved after the capture time stays protected. A malformed row with a recoverable frame ID still counts as present. The percentage and absolute retirement limits then cap what the job can change.

**Where would we get an authoritative list of every frame in a region for this project?**

what are the options

There are four practical options for establishing what a complete snapshot contains.

| Option | How it works | What it requires |
|---|---|---|
| **Trusted exporter with a manifest** | The upstream system exports the whole scope from a consistent read and produces a manifest with the scope, capture time, expected count, and CSV checksum. | We can change the exporter and verify where the manifest came from. The operator can still upload the files through the app. |
| **Import directly from the source** | The app fetches the complete inventory from an upstream API and verifies that it reached the end of a single, consistent snapshot. | The API supports a point-in-time export or stable pagination. Fetching every page of a changing list can miss frames. |
| **Check against an authoritative frame ID list** | The CSV supplies row details. A separate, trusted list supplies the complete set of frame IDs for the same scope and capture time. The importer checks that the sets match. | We have a reliable source for that ID list. This keeps the legacy CSV format intact. |
| **Review retirements explicitly** | Import the CSV as DELTA and show an operator which frames are missing. The operator reviews and explicitly selects any frames to retire. | Someone can verify those removals. This supports a manual workflow when the source can’t prove completeness. |

For this exercise, a **controlled local exporter** could generate a CSV and manifest from seeded source data. That would let us test incomplete files, stale snapshots, and retirement end to end. Real inventory would still need an authoritative source for the completeness claim.

content.text: what are the options?
what are the options?

A complete Region A snapshot tells us the frame is no longer in A. Here are the options for deciding what happens to the frame itself.

| Option | What happens when Region A arrives first | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| **Retire, then reactivate** | Retire the frame when A’s snapshot is applied. Reactivate it in B when B’s later snapshot arrives, keeping both changes in history. | Simple to implement. The frame can temporarily disappear from the default inventory list. |
| **Wait for a matching batch** | Hold the retirement until all regional exports from the same capture are available. If B contains the frame, record a move. | Avoids temporary retirement. A missing or delayed regional export can hold up the batch. |
| **Have the exporter identify moves** | The exporter supplies signed evidence that the frame moved to B. A’s import protects it from retirement until B’s snapshot can apply the move. | Regional imports can run independently. The exporter needs visibility across regions and a way to identify departures. |
| **Review ambiguous absences manually** | Keep the frame active and show the absence for review. An operator can confirm a retirement or wait for B’s export. | Works with region-only data. Adds a review step for absences the exporter can’t explain. |

what are the options?

There are three ways to confirm a retirement. Each gives the importer a different kind of evidence.

| Option | Evidence | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| **Explicit withdrawal from the source** | The source records that the frame ID was withdrawn or decommissioned. The exporter includes that event and its effective time in the signed manifest. | Clear audit trail. Requires the source to retain withdrawal records. |
| **Absence from a complete global capture** | The exporter checks the frame against every region in one consistent capture and signs a statement that it’s absent from the whole inventory. | Works when the source removes records without recording a withdrawal. It requires a complete global view, even for a regional export. |
| **Operator confirmation** | The importer flags the unexplained absence. An operator checks the source and explicitly retires the frame. | Works with regional CSVs alone. Adds manual work and depends on what the operator can verify. |

Seeing the frame missing from two consecutive regional exports can help prioritize review. Both exports can omit it for the same reason, such as a move or a persistent export filter.

| Option | When it fits | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| **1–2 hours** | Snapshots are generated on demand and uploaded right away. | Limits how much the source can change before apply. A queue delay can force a fresh export. |

content.text: what are the options?
what are the options?

The 10% guard can stay. An absolute cap bounds how many frames can retire, and a time limit bounds how long the snapshot can hold up other writes. These numbers are starting points to benchmark.

| Option | Example limits | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| **One cap for every scope** | 100 retirements per job, 1 second to acquire the lock, and 5 seconds to apply once acquired. | Simple to reason about. A legitimate larger retirement needs a separate workflow. |
| **Caps by scope** | 50 for an environment, 100 for a region, and 250 for a country, with the same lock deadline for all three. | Gives broader exports more room. Each cap needs testing, and the time limit can still stop a smaller job. |
| **Retire in batches** | Up to 100 retirements per transaction, with a short lock deadline per batch. | Lets other writes run between batches. It changes the current all-or-nothing design because a job can stop after some retirements have committed. |

The apply deadline matters even when **zero** frames retire. A snapshot can still update thousands of present rows. With either single-transaction option, exceeding the deadline would roll back inventory changes and leave the watermark unchanged.

---
name: egm-synthesizer
description: Intermediate Swarm Compiler and Aggregator coordinating parallel Goldfish reviewers, deduplicating findings, and compiling deliverable reports.
license: Apache-2.0
---

# Core Mandates (Swarm Compiler & Output Synthesizer)

You are the **EGM Synthesizer Persona**. You serve as an intermediate orchestrator and technical compiler between the root agent (the Elephant) and the swarm of stateless Goldfish subagents.

1. **Subagent Delegation**: When requested by the Elephant, you spawn and coordinate the individual Goldfish subagents using your harness's subagent tool.
2. **Output Offloading & Normalization**: The Goldfish subagents report raw findings in unconstrained natural language. You take full responsibility for normalizing their feedback, deduplicating overlapping points, grouping findings by severity (🔴 Blocker, 🟡 Major, 🟢 Nit), and normalizing file line references.
3. **Artifact-First Delivery**: You format the consolidated feedback into a polished Markdown document and write it directly to the workspace or artifact directory using your file-writing tool.
4. **Clean Handoff**: You send a single, concise completion message back to the Elephant with the artifact link or path.

---

# Role

You are **EGM Synthesizer**.
You are an expert Multi-Agent Coordinator and Technical Editor. You bridge the gap between divergent, specialized Goldfish analyzers and the high-level Elephant partner by transforming raw, multi-perspective feedback into a structured, unified deliverable.

---

# Instructions

Inspect the `Mode` parameter specified by the caller (`Mode: BRAINSTORM` vs `Mode: REVIEW`):

## IF Mode: BRAINSTORM (Upstream Concept Ideation)
1. **Subagent Spawning**: Launch the parallel Goldfish swarm across the 7 specialized lenses (`design_critic`, `codebase_details`, `zoom_out`, `comprehension`, `implementation_readiness`, `structural`, `inventive_catalyst`), passing `Mode: BRAINSTORM` and `FeatureConcept: [FeatureConcept]`. Set role titles ending in `-Brainstormer` (e.g., `Skeptical Architect Brainstormer`, `UX & Ergonomics Brainstormer`, `Inventive Catalyst Brainstormer`).
   * **Failed Reviewers**: A reviewer that times out, fails, or returns no report did not review. Retry it once. If it fails again, its status is `not run` in `concepts_brief.md`. Never count it as a lens with zero findings.
2. **Aggregate & Synthesize Concept Brief**: Collect findings from all 7 Goldfish, deduplicate overlapping points, synthesize inventive contradictions and pattern resolutions alongside risk dimensions, and compile them into `concepts_brief.md`.
3. **Write Deliverable**: Write the synthesized brief to `concepts_brief.md` using your file-writing tool.
4. **Notify Elephant**: Send a completion message to the Elephant with the `concepts_brief.md` path.

## IF Mode: REVIEW (Document Audit)
* **Personas Directory**: `agents/{name}.md`
* **Document Standards Directory**: `resources/document_standards/{standard_name}.md`

1. **Subagent Spawning**: Launch the requested subagents in the `Reviewers` list (optionally launching two independent instances, A and B, for each reviewer to maximize finding recall and eliminate non-deterministic evaluation gaps).
   * **Failed Reviewers**: A reviewer that times out, fails, or returns no report did not review. Retry it once. If it fails again, its status is `not run`. Never count it as a reviewer with zero findings.
2. **Aggregate & Triage**: Group reported findings from all subagent instances into 🔴 **Blocker**, 🟡 **Major**, and 🟢 **Nit**. Deduplicate overlapping findings and normalize file references.
3. **Format Review Report**: Format the consolidated findings according to this Markdown layout:

   ```markdown
   # Goldfish Review Report

   **Target:** `[TargetFile]` (`[LineRange]`)

   ## Reviewer Status

   | Reviewer | Status |
   | --- | --- |
   | `[agent-shortname]` | [completed \| not run] |

   ## Prioritized Findings (Blockers -> Major -> Nits)

   ### [Issue Name] - Severity: [Blocker | Major | Nit]
   * **Reviewer Lens:** `[agent-shortname]`
   * **Affected Scope:** `[Lines Start-End]` (or section header)
   * **Discrepancy Description**: [Precise technical, structural, or clarity gap.]
   * **Rationale & Recommendation**: [Concise, objective reason and guidance.]
   ```

4. **Write Artifact**: Write findings to the report file the caller names (`goldfish_review_report.md` if none) using your file-writing tool.
5. **Notify Elephant**: Send a completion message to the Elephant with the status (`completed` or `not run`) of each requested reviewer, the severity breakdown, and the artifact link.

---

# Output Format

Always produce the deliverable artifact file (`goldfish_review_report.md` or `concepts_brief.md`) before sending the completion notification back to the primary agent.
# Harnesses

EGM is one set of skills and personas. This repository serves as the
plugin source for each supported harness. No harness gets a fork of the skill
text.

## Install

| Harness | Install |
| --- | --- |
| ChatGPT desktop | Install the [published EGM plugin](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugins_6aeb90f47ec88191a3c107e01d3eb357) (desktop-only listing); see [packaging](codex.md#test-a-local-package) for personal testing |
| Codex desktop | Install the [published EGM plugin](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugins_6aeb90f47ec88191a3c107e01d3eb357) (desktop-only listing) |
| Antigravity CLI | `agy plugin install https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model` |
| Antigravity App | Run `/plugin` or see [installation instructions](#antigravity-app-and-antigravity-for-ides) |
| Antigravity for IDEs | Run `/plugin` or see [installation instructions](#antigravity-app-and-antigravity-for-ides) |
| Antigravity IDE (standalone) | Not supported; see [installation instructions](#antigravity-app-and-antigravity-for-ides) |
| Claude Code | `claude plugin marketplace add google/elephant-goldfish-model && claude plugin install egm@egm` |
| Claude Cowork | Install from claude.ai/plugins or the Cowork plugin panel via marketplace `google/elephant-goldfish-model` |
| Codex CLI | `codex plugin marketplace add google/elephant-goldfish-model && codex plugin add egm@egm` |
| ChatGPT workspace import | Admin > Plugins > Add > Import marketplace, repo URL `https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model`, path `.agents/plugins`; cloud review limits still apply |
| omp | `omp plugin marketplace add google/elephant-goldfish-model && omp plugin install egm@egm` |
| Muse | `git clone https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model.git && muse plugins install ./elephant-goldfish-model --scope user && muse plugins approve egm` |

Install the whole plugin. Skill-only installers that copy `skills/` alone
break EGM, because the skills read `agents/` and
`resources/document_standards/` at run time.

### Antigravity App and Antigravity for IDEs

- **Antigravity App**: Run `/plugin`, ask the agent `Install https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model`, or manually install into `~/.gemini/config/plugins/egm/` using the commands below.
- **Antigravity for IDEs (Extension for Visual Studio Code)**: Run `/plugin`, ask the agent `Install https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model`, or manually install into `~/.gemini/config/plugins/egm/` using the commands below.
- **Antigravity IDE (Standalone)**: Not supported at this time. Although the plugin and skills load from `~/.gemini/config/plugins/egm/`, standalone Antigravity IDE (tested on macOS and Linux) does not expose the fresh-context subagent tool (`invoke_subagent`) required for Goldfish reviews (`/egm-brainstorm` and `/egm-review`).

The Antigravity App and Antigravity for IDEs share the global plugin directory
`~/.gemini/config/plugins/<name>/`. For a fresh manual installation without the
`agy` CLI, copy the full runtime bundle into `~/.gemini/config/plugins/egm/`
(copying into an existing plugin directory can leave obsolete files behind, so
remove `~/.gemini/config/plugins/egm` first when updating):

```sh
git clone https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model.git
cd elephant-goldfish-model
mkdir -p ~/.gemini/config/plugins/egm
cp -R plugin.json README.md LICENSE skills agents resources docs assets ~/.gemini/config/plugins/egm/
```

Reload the window (or restart the Antigravity App), then confirm that `egm`
appears in the plugin list and that its skills (`egm-brainstorm`, `egm-draft`,
`egm-review`) are available. The command form for these skills in the
Antigravity App and Antigravity for IDEs has not been verified.

## Manifests

Root `plugin.json` is the canonical source for plugin identity, version,
description, and publisher metadata. It follows the portable Agent Plugins
1.0.0 format; the `$schema` key is omitted because omp routes manifests that
declare it to a strict validator that rejects `disable-model-invocation`.
Update shared values there first, then update the compatibility
manifests; unit tests reject metadata drift. Keep platform-specific fields in
their existing manifests until installation tests justify removing them.

Marketplace files are discovery catalogs pointing to this package, not copies
of its skills. In particular, `.agents/plugins/` contains the Codex catalog,
while `agents/` contains reviewer personas. All hosts share the same `skills/`,
`agents/`, and `resources/` content.

| Harness | Manifest | Skills | Subagents |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Antigravity | `plugin.json` | `skills/` (default) | `agents/` (default) |
| Claude Code | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | `skills/` (default) | Claude adapters and orchestrators listed in `plugin.json` `agents` |
| Claude Cowork | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | `skills/` (default) | Subagents run inside Cowork; hooks n/a |
| Codex | `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` | `skills` path | Not shipped; general-purpose subagent reads the persona file |
| ChatGPT | `plugin.json`, `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`; `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` for workspace import | `skills` path | Detect native tools in the current session; general-purpose agent reads the persona |
| omp | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (Claude-compatible fallback) | `skills/` (default) | Personas from `agents/`/`.claude-plugin/agents/` register as native `task` agents |
| Muse | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (Claude-compatible fallback) | `skills/` (default) | 10 adapters import as agents; tool projections unsupported |

Persona prompts live in `agents/`, the directory Antigravity
scans for subagents. Each persona has `name` and `description` frontmatter, so
harnesses that load `agents/*.md` register them as named subagents
(`egm-design`, `egm-zoom-out`, and so on).

When you add a reviewer persona, add a Claude adapter under
`.claude-plugin/agents/` and list it in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`.
The adapter reads the shared persona and sets Claude's read-only tools and
context isolation. This avoids imposing Claude tool names on other hosts.
In Claude Code, `/plugin` > Errors will report that the default `agents/` folder is ignored because the manifest sets `"agents"`; this warning is expected and harmless (see [Claude integration](claude.md#claude-code-warning-default-agents-folder-is-ignored)).

## Delegation

Skills say "spawn a subagent" and name a persona. Each harness maps that
phrase to its own tool:

| Harness | Subagent tool | Named personas | Nesting |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Antigravity | `invoke_subagent` | Yes | Yes |
| Claude Code | Agent (Task) tool | Yes | Up to 3 levels by default |
| Claude Cowork | Cowork subagents | Yes | Subagents run inside Cowork |
| Codex | Native spawn/wait tools; inspect the available schema | No | Detect at runtime; direct dispatch fallback |
| ChatGPT | Native spawn/wait tools when exposed by the current Work session | No | Detect at runtime; direct dispatch fallback |
| omp | `task` tool | Yes | Yes |
| Muse | Native subagents; inspect the available schema | Named spawn rejected in 1.4.14; general-purpose fallback verified | Detect at runtime; direct dispatch fallback |

Where a harness has no named persona, the skill spawns a general-purpose
subagent and tells it to read `agents/<file>.md` first. If a harness cannot
nest subagents, use direct dispatch instead of the synthesizer.

A Goldfish review needs a fresh context. If a harness has no subagent tool,
the review skills stop instead of running in the same context. Check actual
tool availability rather than inferring it from the product name. This applies
to standalone Antigravity IDE and to ChatGPT modes that do not expose native
fresh-context delegation.

Fresh conversation context does not mean that the host omits its instruction
files. Codex's `fork_context: false` and `fork_turns: "none"` isolate parent
turns; they do not establish that project or user instructions are excluded.
Keep stable workspace conventions in instruction files. State review
assumptions that the Goldfish must challenge as explicit review criteria.

## Artifact Directory

Skills write briefs, drafts, and reports to the working directory, or to the
harness's artifact directory if it has one. In Claude Code, Claude Cowork,
Codex, and ChatGPT, you can name another folder. Add this line to your prompt,
or to an agent instructions file that your harness loads (`CLAUDE.md` or
`AGENTS.md`, in the project or at user level):

```text
EGM artifact directory: .dev/docs
```

A relative path is relative to the working directory. If a path set in an
instructions file resolves outside the working directory, after following
symbolic links, EGM asks you to confirm it before creating the folder or
writing there. If you decline or no one can confirm, as in a headless run, the
files go to the working directory. The answer isn't saved, so a new session
asks again. A path in your prompt needs no confirmation. Design docs and other
project files do not move. Claude Code reads a project `AGENTS.md` only when
the project has no `CLAUDE.md`.

Commit approved specifications in `docs/designs/` and project rules in
`AGENTS.md`. Teammates and agents then use the same committed files. Add
`.dev/docs` to `.gitignore` only to keep scratch drafts out of git before
approval.

## Support Status & Contributing Other Harnesses

**Antigravity CLI**, **Claude Code**, and **Codex** pass automated installation
and end-to-end workflow fixtures. Reviewer isolation evidence is narrower:
parent-turn isolation and host-instruction exclusion are separate results.

Claude reviewer adapters set `omitClaudeMd: true`; see the
[Claude integration](claude.md#reviewer-isolation). For Codex, issue [#237](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/issues/237)
reports that Codex CLI 0.166.0 supplied project and user `AGENTS.md` files
despite `fork_turns: "none"`. For Antigravity CLI, the same issue reports
project `AGENTS.md` and `GEMINI.md` in reviewer context. These are reported
host-instruction leaks, not evidence that parent conversation turns leaked.
The Codex test and recorded Antigravity run check parent-turn isolation only;
neither verifies instruction-file exclusion. No host-specific exclusion
control is verified here for Codex or Antigravity.

**Claude Cowork** ([#105](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/issues/105)) and **ChatGPT Work** ([#106](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/issues/106)) have working installation paths with open cloud trace verification gaps. The README's prefix guidance covers only Antigravity (agy CLI), Claude Code, and Codex. For ChatGPT workspace imports, the skills are reached through `@egm` (see [ChatGPT](codex.md#chatgpt)); the command form in Claude Cowork is not recorded yet.

**omp** ([#186](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/issues/186)) has a working installation path. Skills are invoked as `/skill:egm-<command>` (omp registers one command per skill; it has no `/egm-*` namespace). Community-verified on omp v18.12.6: all seven skills discover and resolve, and all nine reviewer personas register as subagents. End-to-end workflow fixtures are not yet automated for omp.

In omp, `skill://` reads are confined to each skill's own folder and reject `..` traversal, so plugin-root assets (`resources/`, `agents/`, `docs/`) cannot be read through `skill://` paths ([#455](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/issues/455)). Until a dedicated omp adapter lands under [#186](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/issues/186), resolve the physical plugin root two directories above the skill folder (for example via `realpath skill://<name>` or the physical path printed in the header of `read skill://<name>`) and read plugin-root assets by absolute path.

**Muse** (1.4.14) has a working installation path. `muse plugins validate` reports the plugin valid with all seven skills and all ten agent adapters supported; every agent tool projection is unsupported, so Claude tool allowlists do not restrict Muse reviewers. Install from a local path; `marketplace add` on this repository discovers zero plugins because Muse reads the Codex catalog first. End-to-end workflow fixtures passed on 2026-10-30 (brainstorm, draft, and uninterrupted review with 15 fresh-context reviewers); named `egm/egm-*` agents cannot be spawned in this runtime, so reviewers used the general-purpose fallback reading the installed persona first. See the [Muse guide](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/blob/main/docs/muse.md). No skill routes a Muse session to that guide yet ([#252](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/issues/252)), so point the session at it.

**Windsurf** (renamed Devin Desktop on 2026-06-02; [#376](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/issues/376)) has experimental workspace routing. The rule and workflow files resolve the shared `skills/*/SKILL.md`, `agents/*.md`, and `resources/document_standards/*.md` files directly. They do not copy skill text. Goldfish reviews stop if fresh-context, read-only subagent delegation is unavailable, and reviewers launch on the host's read-only subagent profile. Devin CLI 3000.12.43 runs on 2026-11-10 passed routing, human pauses, read-only reviewers, and parent-marker isolation with every file write denied, so no workflow ran to a final artifact. Devin Desktop and the Devin CLI run the same agent, Devin Local, which replaced Cascade. The Devin Desktop IDE remains untested. The CLI does not list `.windsurf/workflows/` as slash commands; `/egm-*` requests route through the rule. Denying a permission prompt ends the host's turn without a message; send a follow-up message to continue. See the [design](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/blob/main/docs/designs/windsurf_support.md#recorded-cli-evidence-2026-11-10) for the evidence.

See the [harness test record](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/blob/main/TESTING.md#harness-test-record) for tested surfaces and limits.

We welcome contributors who want to help verify and expand harness support.

### Contributing Support for New Harnesses

A harness counts as supported after `/egm-brainstorm`, `/egm-draft`, and
`/egm-review` run end to end through its plugin install. When contributing
support for another harness:

1. Add the appropriate manifest or configuration file to the repository root
   (e.g., matching the harness's plugin/extension standard).
2. Document install steps, manifest mapping, and delegation mechanics in this guide
   (`docs/harnesses.md`).
3. Verify that `/egm-brainstorm`, `/egm-draft`, and `/egm-review` run end to end,

# Core Mandates (Swarm Compiler & Output Synthesizer)

You are the **EGM Synthesizer Persona**. You serve as an intermediate orchestrator and technical compiler between the root agent (the Elephant) and the swarm of stateless Goldfish subagents.

1. **Subagent Delegation**: When requested by the Elephant, you spawn and coordinate the individual Goldfish subagents using your harness's subagent tool.
2. **Output Offloading & Normalization**: The Goldfish subagents report raw findings in unconstrained natural language. You take full responsibility for normalizing their feedback, deduplicating overlapping points, grouping findings by severity (🔴 Blocker, 🟡 Major, 🟢 Nit), and normalizing file line references.
3. **Artifact-First Delivery**: You format the consolidated feedback into a polished Markdown document and write it directly to the workspace or artifact directory using your file-writing tool.
4. **Clean Handoff**: You send a single, concise completion message back to the Elephant with the artifact link or path.

---

# Role

You are **EGM Synthesizer**.
You are an expert Multi-Agent Coordinator and Technical Editor. You bridge the gap between divergent, specialized Goldfish analyzers and the high-level Elephant partner by transforming raw, multi-perspective feedback into a structured, unified deliverable.

---

# Instructions

Inspect the `Mode` parameter specified by the caller (`Mode: BRAINSTORM` vs `Mode: REVIEW`):

## IF Mode: BRAINSTORM (Upstream Concept Ideation)
1. **Subagent Spawning**: Launch the parallel Goldfish swarm across the 7 specialized lenses (`design_critic`, `codebase_details`, `zoom_out`, `comprehension`, `implementation_readiness`, `structural`, `inventive_catalyst`), passing `Mode: BRAINSTORM` and `FeatureConcept: [FeatureConcept]`. Set role titles ending in `-Brainstormer` (e.g., `Skeptical Architect Brainstormer`, `UX & Ergonomics Brainstormer`, `Inventive Catalyst Brainstormer`).
   * **Failed Reviewers**: A reviewer that times out, fails, or returns no report did not review. Retry it once. If it fails again, its status is `not run` in `concepts_brief.md`. Never count it as a lens with zero findings.
2. **Aggregate & Synthesize Concept Brief**: Collect findings from all 7 Goldfish, deduplicate overlapping points, synthesize inventive contradictions and pattern resolutions alongside risk dimensions, and compile them into `concepts_brief.md`.
3. **Write Deliverable**: Write the synthesized brief to `concepts_brief.md` using your file-writing tool.
4. **Notify Elephant**: Send a completion message to the Elephant with the `concepts_brief.md` path.

## IF Mode: REVIEW (Document Audit)
* **Personas Directory**: `agents/{name}.md`
* **Document Standards Directory**: `resources/document_standards/{standard_name}.md`

1. **Subagent Spawning**: Launch the requested subagents in the `Reviewers` list (optionally launching two independent instances, A and B, for each reviewer to maximize finding recall and eliminate non-deterministic evaluation gaps).
   * **Failed Reviewers**: A reviewer that times out, fails, or returns no report did not review. Retry it once. If it fails again, its status is `not run`. Never count it as a reviewer with zero findings.
2. **Aggregate & Triage**: Group reported findings from all subagent instances into 🔴 **Blocker**, 🟡 **Major**, and 🟢 **Nit**. Deduplicate overlapping findings and normalize file references.
3. **Format Review Report**: Format the consolidated findings according to this Markdown layout:

   ```markdown
   # Goldfish Review Report

   **Target:** `[TargetFile]` (`[LineRange]`)

   ## Reviewer Status

   | Reviewer | Status |
   | --- | --- |
   | `[agent-shortname]` | [completed \| not run] |

   ## Prioritized Findings (Blockers -> Major -> Nits)

   ### [Issue Name] - Severity: [Blocker | Major | Nit]
   * **Reviewer Lens:** `[agent-shortname]`
   * **Affected Scope:** `[Lines Start-End]` (or section header)
   * **Discrepancy Description**: [Precise technical, structural, or clarity gap.]
   * **Rationale & Recommendation**: [Concise, objective reason and guidance.]
   ```

4. **Write Artifact**: Write findings to the report file the caller names (`goldfish_review_report.md` if none) using your file-writing tool.
5. **Notify Elephant**: Send a completion message to the Elephant with the status (`completed` or `not run`) of each requested reviewer, the severity breakdown, and the artifact link.

---

# Output Format

Always produce the deliverable artifact file (`goldfish_review_report.md` or `concepts_brief.md`) before sending the completion notification back to the primary agent.

cat > "$review_dir/snapshot-contract.md" <<'EOF'
# FULL_SNAPSHOT safety contract under review

Author: Alex Callow  
Issue: GLO-34, Define the FULL_SNAPSHOT safety contract  
Status: Working hypothesis for Goldfish review

## Purpose

DELTA can update rows supplied by an operator. FULL_SNAPSHOT adds versioned retirement for frames that the upstream source confirmed were withdrawn. It also needs to handle frames that leave one region and appear in another, out-of-order exports, and competing manual edits. The exercise can run this locally with a controlled exporter and a dataset separate from the app inventory. A real rollout depends on an authoritative upstream producer.

## Export evidence

A trusted exporter reads one complete, consistent source scope. Its signed manifest identifies the canonical scope, UTC capture time, expected logical record count from the source read, and SHA-256 checksum of the CSV. The importer verifies the producer, signed fields, row count, and exact bytes of the pinned S3 object version before inventory writes. The manifest capture time is the watermark. The draft scopes are GLOBAL, country, country/region, and country/region/environment. An environment requires a country and a region.

The manifest also carries known lifecycle events. A move identifies the frame ID, origin and destination. A withdrawal identifies the frame ID, last known scope, and effective time. A reinstatement identifies the frame ID, destination scope, and effective time. The producer signs those claims with the snapshot. A real source must be able to establish scope completeness and these lifecycle events.

## Snapshot admission and ordering

Reject capture times in the future, and reject snapshots older than 24 hours. Check age at manifest verification and again before apply against the backend UTC clock. A job that ages out in the queue fails with SNAPSHOT_TOO_OLD. A rejected snapshot leaves inventory and the watermark unchanged.

For the same scope and capture time, identical signed contents and matching CSV bytes return the previous result without creating versions. Different signed contents at the same capture time are a conflict. Leave the previous result in place, identify its job, and require a fresh capture. Apply the original design's scope hierarchy for ordered watermarks. Reject a narrower snapshot older than a committed ancestor. Protect a newer descendant scope from retirement by a broader snapshot. Present rows still follow normal conflict checks under the original broader-snapshot rule.

## Scope validation and lifecycle behavior

A row outside the signed scope or with a malformed field needed to verify its scope fails the snapshot. A row with no recoverable frame ID also fails the snapshot. An identifiable row with a malformed field unrelated to scope protects that frame from retirement and counts toward the 5% malformed-row limit. A header-only or unrecoverable file failure leaves inventory and the watermark unchanged.

When an origin snapshot arrives before the destination, a signed move keeps the frame active at its last known location and reports that the destination import is pending. When the destination snapshot applies the move, append a new active version in that scope. Arrival in the reverse order must yield the same active frame and no intermediate retirement. An unexplained absence keeps the frame active and is shown in diagnostics.

Automatic retirement requires a signed withdrawal effective by the capture time. Protect a frame with a newer edit or move. Reject a snapshot that includes both a live row and a withdrawal for one frame. Retirement appends a RETIRED version with the withdrawal and job lineage. Retired frames remain visible through explicit filtering, direct lookup, and history. Ordinary edit and delete requests reject a snapshot-retired frame.

Reactivation requires a valid row in the destination scope and a signed reinstatement effective after the withdrawal and by the capture time. Protect newer manual actions. Append a new active version even when the row's details are unchanged. The existing DELTA force-overwrite rule still applies to manually deleted frames.

## Apply boundaries

Stage and validate the file outside the inventory lock. Recheck scope, lifecycle ordering and retirement eligibility against the protected pre-apply view. Use a single transaction to commit inventory versions, the job result, and the scope watermark. Before writing, reject if malformed rows exceed 5% or eligible retirements exceed the smaller of 100 frames and 10% of all pre-apply active frames in scope. Active means a current version in LIVE, PENDING, MAINTENANCE, BLOCKED, or DRAFT. The same set defines retirement eligibility. Manually deleted frames have no current version.

Wait at most 1 second to acquire the exclusive inventory lock. Let the worker retry contention within the freshness limit. Once the lock is acquired, allow at most 5 seconds for the full apply and roll back on timeout. Benchmark with a 10,000-row snapshot and competing manual writes before rollout. The existing 10 MiB and 10,000-row CSV limits apply.

## Verification examples

- Seed 100 frames in the app and issue three upstream withdrawals. A complete 97-row export retires exactly those three. Truncate that same export and check that the importer rejects it before inventory changes.
- Import Region A before B, then repeat on clean data with B first. Both orders end with the frame active in B and no intermediate RETIRED version.
- Submit an exact replay, a same-time conflict, an old or future capture, an unscopable row, a live row contradicting a withdrawal, and a reinstatement with an unchanged valid row.
- Exercise guard boundaries, the lock wait and apply deadlines, and rollback before advancing the watermark. Verify DELTA behavior and version history.
EOF
printf '%s\\n' "$review_dir"`});store("goldfishDir",r.output.trim());text(r);

### Decisions for the author

- **Blocker — Define per-frame lifecycle ordering** (lines 15, 27–31). A fresh capture can carry an old withdrawal after the frame has already been reinstated. A move has no effective time or stable event identity, so delayed destination imports cannot reliably distinguish an old move from the latest one. Require stable event identities and monotonic, per-frame source ordering. Persist the accepted lifecycle state and define how contradictory claims, stale events, and out-of-order moves are handled.
- **Blocker — Define which manual actions block a lifecycle change** (lines 21, 29–35). A withdrawal effective at 09:00, a manual edit at 09:30, and a capture at 10:00 produce different results depending on which upstream timestamp the importer compares. Specify the comparison and tie rules for moves, withdrawals, and reinstatements. Require each decision to use the current version and its provenance inside the transaction.
- **Major — Decide how to retire the last frames in a scope** (lines 25, 35). Retiring one of nine active frames exceeds the 10% cap, and withdrawing every source frame yields a header-only export that always fails. Decide whether to support a signed zero-row export and define how operators resolve legitimate withdrawals above the cap.
- **Major — Resolve overlapping captures and late replays** (lines 19–21). Equal capture times conflict only within a scope, so overlapping scopes can disagree at the same instant. Exact replay also promises the previous result while the age rule rejects captures older than 24 hours. Specify the authority and tie rules across overlapping scopes, and whether returning an existing result is subject to freshness.

### Implementation requirements

- **Major — Validate unique frame identities and lifecycle claims before apply** (lines 13–15, 25–35). A byte checksum and record count can both pass with duplicate frame IDs. Define duplicate handling, scope matching for each event, and the outcome when an identifiable malformed row also has a withdrawal. Include those cases in the acceptance checks.
- **Major — Benchmark the cost of the protected transaction** (lines 35–37). A 10,000-row file still leaves the active inventory and manifest event list unbounded. Set manifest byte and event limits, define how sources larger than 10,000 rows are supported, and benchmark representative inventory size and lifecycle-event volume under concurrent writes. Verify that every inventory writer participates in the same transaction or lock protocol.

1. **Enforce the lifecycle contract across DELTA, snapshots, and manual writes.** The DELTA candidate query allows any current version to be replaced by a newer source row or a forced correction. Manual edits and deletes check the current version ID without checking its status. Once snapshots can create `RETIRED` versions, these paths can bypass signed reinstatement. Define a transition matrix, enforce it under the stable-frame lock, and expose distinct rejection reasons. Give moves an effective time or source sequence and define how lifecycle order compares with source-row timestamps and newer manual writes. Add tests for forced DELTA against retired frames, both move arrival orders, and lifecycle lineage without changing the existing DELTA payload hash. The DELTA hash includes most `frame_version` columns, so adding lineage columns requires an explicit hash projection or separate lineage storage. [delta-candidates.sql:7](src/backend/src/main/resources/inventory-import/delta-candidates.sql#L7), [FrameService.java:77](src/backend/src/main/java/com/global/ct/frameinventory/frame/FrameService.java#L77)

2. **Stage scope evidence independently of row validity.** The parser stops at the first invalid field, and malformed rows retain only their ID and error. For example, an invalid status can hide a missing or out-of-scope region. Extract and stage scope evidence independently and use the same canonical membership rules for staged rows, current inventory, and signed events. Specify treatment of missing geography and environment, which the existing model can store. Test an identifiable row with both an invalid status and an out-of-scope region. 3. **Give lock contention, apply overruns, and freshness expiry distinct outcomes.** The inventory lock currently has only blocking shared acquisition. The worker’s `Apply` result is a boolean that distinguishes completion from restaging, and exhausted retries become `IMPORT_PROCESSING_FAILED`. Define a retryable lock-wait outcome and terminal apply-timeout and freshness outcomes. Enforce the one-second wait and five-second full-apply budgets in the backend transaction, including rollback and lock release. Instrument wait and lock-held durations separately, and verify both watermark rollback and manual-write recovery under contention. [InventoryWriteLock.java:14](src/backend/src/main/java/com/global/ct/frameinventory/common/InventoryWriteLock.java#L14), [import_worker.proto:30](src/backend/src/main/proto/frameinventory/v1/import_worker.proto#L30), [workflow.py:29](src/workflows/inventory_workflows/workflow.py#L29)

Row diagnostics require a positive CSV record number, so they cannot represent absent frames, pending destinations, or protected descendants. Add job-level guard and ordering diagnostics and frame-level lifecycle diagnostics without CSV row numbers. Persist the verified producer and manifest identity, pinned object version, canonical scope, capture time, guard numerator and denominator, and original result reference. Specify replay precedence over age and watermark checks, how failed attempts affect replay, and who may see another owner’s job reference. The existing dashboard covers backlog, dispatch failures, and overall apply duration. Require linked trace context or structured events keyed by job ID across upload binding, Temporal attempts, manifest verification, and transaction outcome. Message Type: FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: /root
Sender: /root/readiness
Payload:
The hypothesis needs three decisions before `FULL_SNAPSHOT` can safely write inventory versions.

1. **Blocker — Lifecycle ordering across scopes and manual edits (lines 15, 21, 27–31).** Moves have no effective time or source sequence. Scope watermarks alone cannot resolve a move, withdrawal, or reinstatement reported by overlapping exports. Define a per-frame event identity and ordering rule, how equal-time conflicts are handled, which scopes may apply each event, and how source events compare with manual edits and deletions. Verify both arrival orders for a move, repeated events across scopes, an older withdrawal after a move or reinstatement, and a manual edit between staging and apply. Assert the resulting scope, status, and version history.

2. **Blocker — `RETIRED` compatibility and rollback (lines 29–37).** Once the first retirement commits, existing API consumers, inventory readers, and rollback builds may encounter a status they cannot interpret. Deploy compatible storage and readers before enabling snapshot writes. Specify how DELTA, including force-overwrite, handles a snapshot-retired frame. Define an operator switch to stop snapshot writes while retaining compatible readers and committed history. Verify list, direct lookup, history, edit, delete, and DELTA against a stored `RETIRED` version, then disable snapshot writes and repeat those checks.

3. **Blocker — Concurrent apply and durable replay (lines 19–21, 35–37).** Define which operations participate in the inventory lock, including manual mutations and DELTA. Recheck freshness, replay identity, and scope watermarks after acquisition. State whether an old exact replay can return a committed result, and whether a failed attempt reserves the scope and capture time. Persist the replay identity with the job result so a worker can recover after losing the commit acknowledgement. Verify simultaneous exact replays, overlapping snapshots, expiry while waiting for the lock, timeout after partial work, and retry after a lost acknowledgement. Assert that inventory versions, the result, and the watermark commit together and only once.

Two details belong in the design before implementation.

- **Major — Manifest compatibility and trust (lines 13–15).** Specify a versioned signed payload, canonical scope and timestamp encoding, producer authorization by scope, and the binding between the verified manifest and the pinned object read by the worker. Define how the exporter keeps the rows and lifecycle claims consistent at capture time. Verify unsupported versions, unauthorized scopes, tampered events, and an S3 key overwritten after staging.
- **Major — Guard boundaries and rollout evidence (lines 25, 35–44).** Define the malformed-row denominator, duplicate-ID handling, and whether retirement limits count distinct frames after protections are applied. Make the operational consequence of rejecting header-only exports explicit when the upstream scope is legitimately empty. Verify exact limits and one item over, independently trigger count and checksum failures with signed fixtures, and run the 10,000-row benchmark with competing manual writes before enabling a trusted producer.

Files read: `implementation_readiness.md`, `implementation-readiness-standard.md`, and `snapshot-contract.md`.

The concept needs two explicit decision tables before implementation. Its verification examples should then pin the observable outcome of each decision.

| Severity | Contract area | Maintainability requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Major | Admission and replay, lines 19–21 | Define the order of signed evidence checks, exact replay, same-capture conflict, freshness checks, and watermark checks. State whether an exact committed replay after 24 hours returns the previous result, and which prior job outcomes can be replayed. Different choices will make retries behave differently after queue delays or a lost response. |
| Major | Scope and lifecycle, lines 13–31 | Define which scopes can assert and apply a move, withdrawal, or reinstatement. Add a per-frame decision table covering current state, effective time, row presence, malformed identifiable rows, and newer edits or moves. Specify how repeated and conflicting events across scopes are resolved, including equal effective times. Add a reference to the original broader-snapshot ordering rule or state the rule here. |
| Major | Protected manual actions, lines 29–35 | Specify how the importer detects a newer manual delete when deletion leaves no current version. Define how delete history participates in snapshot conflict checks and how that differs from the existing DELTA force-overwrite path. Resolve the case where a malformed identifiable row protects a frame that also has a signed withdrawal. |
| Major | Guard evaluation and retries, lines 25 and 33–37 | State which rows count toward the 5% threshold, how exact boundaries are evaluated, and whether protected or already-applied withdrawals enter the retirement count. Specify which failures are retryable and how a failure is recorded after the apply transaction rolls back. Make the header-only rule explicit for a complete zero-row scope with valid withdrawals. |

The purpose already establishes the business problem. The feature draft needs explicit **Goals and Non-Goals**, **Proposed Architecture** covering producer and importer responsibilities, **Alternatives Considered**, and **Risks and Mitigations**. The alternatives should record the concrete trade-offs behind signed withdrawals versus retirement based on complete-snapshot absence, and the exclusive inventory lock versus narrower concurrency control. The risks section should carry forward source authority, overlapping scopes, and the existing rollout benchmark. These sections matter for the feature draft. Heading changes alone are a nit at concept stage.

The verification section should specify each expected job result, inventory and history effect, and watermark effect. Add cases for replay after expiry, stale child and stale parent snapshots with both present and absent rows, stale lifecycle evidence from another scope, newer manual edits and deletions, and a malformed identifiable row paired with a withdrawal. For both guard thresholds, verify the boundary and the first failing count. For contention and apply timeout, verify the retry or terminal result and whether any state committed.

# FULL_SNAPSHOT safety contract and Goldfish review

**Author** — Alex Callow  
**Date** — 2026-11-27  
**Status** — Reviewed working contract. Open decisions are identified below.  
**Scope** — [GLO-34](https://linear.app/upfrontbeats/issue/GLO-34/define-the-full-snapshot-safety-contract) · [Contract reviewed](snapshot-contract.md)

## Overview

FULL_SNAPSHOT lets the app retire a frame after the source confirms its withdrawal. Operators should be able to see why it retired, which snapshot applied the change, and whether a later source event restored it. The local exercise can use a controlled exporter backed by data separate from the app inventory. A real rollout needs a producer that can make the same completeness and lifecycle claims for real inventory.

## Goals and non-goals

- Preserve one active frame and consistent version history when regional imports arrive in either order.
- Require verified source evidence for moves, withdrawals, and reinstatements. Keep unexplained absences visible for review.
- Keep apply atomic and bounded. A failed apply leaves inventory and the scope watermark unchanged.
- Keep deployed identity and permissions in [GLO-28](https://linear.app/upfrontbeats/issue/GLO-28/define-and-implement-import-authorization). GLO-34 defines the contract. [GLO-33](https://linear.app/upfrontbeats/issue/GLO-33/implement-scoped-snapshot-retirement-and-rollout-checks) implements and verifies it.

## Agreed contract

| Area | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Export | A trusted producer reads a complete scope at a consistent point in time. Its signed manifest binds the scope, UTC capture time, expected logical row count and SHA-256 checksum to the pinned CSV bytes. The signature and evidence are checked before inventory writes. |
| Freshness | Reject future captures and new apply attempts older than 24 hours. Check age at manifest verification and again before apply. |
| Same-scope ordering | Return the original result for identical signed contents and CSV bytes. Reject different contents at the same capture time and identify the earlier job. A correction needs a fresh capture. |
| Scope and malformed data | Reject the whole snapshot for out-of-scope rows, an unverifiable required scope field, a missing recoverable frame ID, or an unrecoverable parse error. An identifiable malformed row with verified scope still counts as present. The job fails if more than 5% of logical data records are malformed. |
| Moves | Signed move evidence protects the frame when the origin snapshot arrives first. The valid destination row applies the move. Both arrival orders must end with the frame active in the destination and no intermediate retirement. |
| Withdrawal | Require a signed withdrawal effective by capture time. Protect newer edits or moves. Reject a live row paired with a withdrawal for the same frame. Unexplained absences remain active and show up in diagnostics. |
| Reinstatement | Require a signed reinstatement later than the withdrawal and effective by capture time, plus a valid row in the destination. A newer manual action takes precedence. Matching the old frame details is allowed. |
| Retired frames | Append a RETIRED version with withdrawal and job lineage. Expose it through direct lookup, history and an explicit retired filter. Ordinary edit and delete actions reject it. The existing force rule for manual deletion remains a separate case. |
| Apply limits | Use one transaction. Retire at most the lesser of 100 frames or 10% of pre-apply active frames in scope. Active means a current LIVE, PENDING, MAINTENANCE, BLOCKED, or DRAFT version. Wait at most 1 second for the exclusive inventory lock and allow 5 seconds for the whole apply once acquired. Benchmark a 10,000-row import with competing writes. |

## Analysis

### 1. Blocker — Order lifecycle events across scopes

A newer capture can repeat an older withdrawal. If a frame has already moved or been reinstated, the scope watermark and row timestamp do not tell us which lifecycle event is current. A newer manual edit can also occur after the withdrawal but before the capture. For example, a withdrawal effective at 09:00, a manual edit at 09:30, and a capture at 10:00 give different outcomes depending on the timestamp used.

The reviewers propose a stable signed event ID, an effective time, and a producer-issued sequence that increases per frame across all scopes. Store the accepted order with durable lineage and require the destination export to carry the same move evidence. Specify which scopes can attest to each event, and resolve equal or conflicting event sequences. Decide how source events compare with manual edits and the history of manual deletions. [Reviewed rules](snapshot-contract.md#scope-validation-and-lifecycle-behavior)

The existing hierarchy orders overlapping captures but protects a newer descendant primarily from retirement. Define what an older broad snapshot may do with a present row when either its current scope or destination has newer evidence. Also define equal-time overlap across different scopes. A stale ancestor row must not undo a newer move, withdrawal, or reinstatement. [Earlier hierarchy design](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/docs/designs/bulk-csv-inventory-import-design.md:63)

### 2. Blocker — Preserve the retirement rules across every write path

Today DELTA compares source timestamps and payload hashes, and ordinary frame edits and deletes check the current version ID. Both paths need an explicit guard for snapshot-retired frames, including DELTA force overwrite. The importer must also check the latest history when a manual delete leaves no current version. [DELTA candidate query](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/src/backend/src/main/resources/inventory-import/delta-candidates.sql:7) · [Frame service](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/src/backend/src/main/java/com/global/ct/frameinventory/frame/FrameService.java:77)

Deploy compatible readers, filters, and guards before enabling snapshot writes. The rollout switch should be able to stop new snapshot writes while existing retirement history stays readable. Preserve DELTA replay across the migration. The current payload hash includes most frame-version columns, so adding a lineage column requires an explicit hash projection or separate lineage storage. [DELTA hash](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/src/backend/src/main/resources/inventory-import/delta-candidates.sql:13)

### 3. Blocker — Separate committed replay from new apply

An exact replay may arrive after the 24-hour window, especially after a lost commit response. The reviewers propose returning the durable committed result to an authorized caller while applying freshness to any transaction that can write. Define the snapshot fingerprint, retained verification evidence, result visibility, and whether a failed attempt reserves the scope and capture time.

Under the exclusive lock, recheck freshness, previously committed outcomes, watermarks, and current frame state. Make the one-second lock wait retryable and the five-second apply deadline enforceable across the full transaction. Record contention, timeout, and freshness expiry as distinct outcomes. Local and DELTA writers must continue to use the same lock protocol. [Current shared inventory lock](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/src/backend/src/main/java/com/global/ct/frameinventory/common/InventoryWriteLock.java:14)

### 4. Major — Define recovery when the guard correctly stops a job

One withdrawal in a scope with nine active frames exceeds 10%. A complete export with zero live rows also fails the draft's header-only rule. A fresh export can hit the same limits. Decide whether a signed zero-row export is valid evidence and how operators resolve a legitimate withdrawal the automatic limits block. A proposed recovery is a separate, authorized review of exact candidate IDs and current versions, with a new atomic apply. This recovery is an open decision.

A guard failure should show the eligible retirement count, pre-apply active count, and limit. A pending move should show frame ID, origin, destination, and what clears it if the destination export never arrives or is rejected. Use frame-level diagnostics for absent frames and job-level diagnostics for guards. The current row-error table requires a positive CSV row number. [Existing diagnostic schema](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/src/backend/src/main/resources/db/migration/V3__create_inventory_import.sql:30)

### 5. Major — Make the signed evidence and validation rules precise

Specify a versioned signed format, UTC timestamp encoding, canonical scope identifiers, producer authorization for each scope, and manifest byte and event-count limits. Capture the CSV rows, expected count, and lifecycle facts consistently. A real producer needs stable frame identities across regions and a reliable lifecycle history before retirement is enabled.

Extract scope evidence independently of other validation. The current parser can stop at an invalid status before checking an invalid region. Count each malformed logical record once, and define duplicate-ID and malformed-present-plus-withdrawal behavior explicitly. [Current CSV parser](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/src/backend/src/main/java/com/global/ct/frameinventory/inventoryimport/InventoryCsvReader.java:103)

## Alternatives weighed

- An upstream API or a second authoritative ID list can establish completeness. The signed manifest keeps the existing operator upload flow and lets the producer bind lifecycle evidence to that exact export.
- Retiring at the origin and reactivating at the destination would temporarily hide a valid frame. Waiting for an entire regional batch makes one late region delay the others. Signed move evidence allows independent regional imports.
- Automatic reinstatement based on row presence would make a stray row enough to restore a frame. A signed event provides a dated source decision and supports an unchanged returning row.
- Batched retirement would shorten individual lock holds at the cost of partial commits. The agreed single transaction keeps inventory, the job outcome, and the watermark together.

## Key decisions and staging for next steps

1. Settle per-frame event ordering, scope authority, and precedence over manual changes. Write a lifecycle decision table for move, withdraw, and reinstate.
2. Write an admission and replay table, including committed replay after expiry, a same-time conflict, and an expired or failed uncommitted attempt.
3. Decide how to handle signed empty exports and legitimate above-limit withdrawals. Define what the operator sees and how a blocked change can be resolved.
4. In GLO-33, implement compatible reads and write-path guards before enabling retirement. Verify both move arrival orders, stale broad snapshots, manual changes between staging and apply, manifest tampering, guard boundaries, apply rollback, and lost commit responses. Assert job results, frame history, and watermarks together. Benchmark the full 10,000-row workload under contention before rollout.

## Reviewer status

| Goldfish lens | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Design Critic | Completed |
| Codebase Details | Completed |
| Zoom-Out | Completed |
| Comprehension | Completed |
| Implementation Readiness | Completed |
| Structural | Completed |
| Inventive Catalyst | Completed |

# FULL_SNAPSHOT safety contract and Goldfish review

**Author** — Alex Callow  
**Date** — 2026-11-27  
**Status** — Reviewed working contract. Open decisions are identified below.  
**Scope** — [GLO-34](https://linear.app/upfrontbeats/issue/GLO-34/define-the-full-snapshot-safety-contract) · [Contract reviewed](snapshot-contract.md)

## Overview

FULL_SNAPSHOT lets the app retire a frame after the source confirms its withdrawal. Operators should be able to see why it retired, which snapshot applied the change, and whether a later source event restored it. The local exercise can use a controlled exporter backed by data separate from the app inventory. A real rollout needs a producer that can make the same completeness and lifecycle claims for real inventory.

## Goals and non-goals

- Preserve one active frame and consistent version history when regional imports arrive in either order.
- Require verified source evidence for moves, withdrawals, and reinstatements. Keep unexplained absences visible for review.
- Keep apply atomic and bounded. A failed apply leaves inventory and the scope watermark unchanged.
- Keep deployed identity and permissions in [GLO-28](https://linear.app/upfrontbeats/issue/GLO-28/define-and-implement-import-authorization). GLO-34 defines the contract. [GLO-33](https://linear.app/upfrontbeats/issue/GLO-33/implement-scoped-snapshot-retirement-and-rollout-checks) implements and verifies it.

## Agreed contract

| Area | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Export | A trusted producer reads a complete scope at a consistent point in time. Its signed manifest binds the scope, UTC capture time, expected logical row count and SHA-256 checksum to the pinned CSV bytes. The signature and evidence are checked before inventory writes. |
| Freshness | Reject future captures and new apply attempts older than 24 hours. Check age at manifest verification and again before apply. |
| Same-scope ordering | Return the original result for identical signed contents and CSV bytes. Reject different contents at the same capture time and identify the earlier job. A correction needs a fresh capture. |
| Scope and malformed data | Reject the whole snapshot for out-of-scope rows, an unverifiable required scope field, a missing recoverable frame ID, or an unrecoverable parse error. An identifiable malformed row with verified scope still counts as present. The job fails if more than 5% of logical data records are malformed. |
| Moves | Signed move evidence protects the frame when the origin snapshot arrives first. The valid destination row applies the move. Both arrival orders must end with the frame active in the destination and no intermediate retirement. |
| Withdrawal | Require a signed withdrawal effective by capture time. Protect newer edits or moves. Reject a live row paired with a withdrawal for the same frame. Unexplained absences remain active and show up in diagnostics. |
| Reinstatement | Require a signed reinstatement later than the withdrawal and effective by capture time, plus a valid row in the destination. A newer manual action takes precedence. Matching the old frame details is allowed. |
| Retired frames | Append a RETIRED version with withdrawal and job lineage. Expose it through direct lookup, history and an explicit retired filter. Ordinary edit and delete actions reject it. The existing force rule for manual deletion remains a separate case. |
| Apply limits | Use one transaction. Retire at most the lesser of 100 frames or 10% of pre-apply active frames in scope. Active means a current LIVE, PENDING, MAINTENANCE, BLOCKED, or DRAFT version. Wait at most 1 second for the exclusive inventory lock and allow 5 seconds for the whole apply once acquired. Benchmark a 10,000-row import with competing writes. |

## Analysis

### 1. Blocker — Order lifecycle events across scopes

A newer capture can repeat an older withdrawal. If a frame has already moved or been reinstated, the scope watermark and row timestamp do not tell us which lifecycle event is current. A newer manual edit can also occur after the withdrawal but before the capture. For example, a withdrawal effective at 09:00, a manual edit at 09:30, and a capture at 10:00 give different outcomes depending on the timestamp used.

The reviewers propose a stable signed event ID, an effective time, and a producer-issued sequence that increases per frame across all scopes. Store the accepted order with durable lineage and require the destination export to carry the same move evidence. Specify which scopes can attest to each event, and resolve equal or conflicting event sequences. Decide how source events compare with manual edits and the history of manual deletions. [Reviewed rules](snapshot-contract.md#scope-validation-and-lifecycle-behavior)

The existing hierarchy orders overlapping captures but protects a newer descendant primarily from retirement. Define what an older broad snapshot may do with a present row when either its current scope or destination has newer evidence. Also define equal-time overlap across different scopes. A stale ancestor row must not undo a newer move, withdrawal, or reinstatement. [Earlier hierarchy design](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/docs/designs/bulk-csv-inventory-import-design.md:63)

### 2. Blocker — Preserve the retirement rules across every write path

Today DELTA compares source timestamps and payload hashes, and ordinary frame edits and deletes check the current version ID. Both paths need an explicit guard for snapshot-retired frames, including DELTA force overwrite. The importer must also check the latest history when a manual delete leaves no current version. [DELTA candidate query](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/src/backend/src/main/resources/inventory-import/delta-candidates.sql:7) · [Frame service](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/src/backend/src/main/java/com/global/ct/frameinventory/frame/FrameService.java:77)

Deploy compatible readers, filters, and guards before enabling snapshot writes. The rollout switch should be able to stop new snapshot writes while existing retirement history stays readable. Preserve DELTA replay across the migration. The current payload hash includes most frame-version columns, so adding a lineage column requires an explicit hash projection or separate lineage storage. [DELTA hash](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/src/backend/src/main/resources/inventory-import/delta-candidates.sql:13)

### 3. Blocker — Separate committed replay from new apply

An exact replay may arrive after the 24-hour window, especially after a lost commit response. The reviewers propose returning the durable committed result to an authorized caller while applying freshness to any transaction that can write. Define the snapshot fingerprint, retained verification evidence, result visibility, and whether a failed attempt reserves the scope and capture time.

Under the exclusive lock, recheck freshness, previously committed outcomes, watermarks, and current frame state. Make the one-second lock wait retryable and the five-second apply deadline enforceable across the full transaction. Record contention, timeout, and freshness expiry as distinct outcomes. Local and DELTA writers must continue to use the same lock protocol. [Current shared inventory lock](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/src/backend/src/main/java/com/global/ct/frameinventory/common/InventoryWriteLock.java:14)

### 4. Major — Define recovery when the guard correctly stops a job

One withdrawal in a scope with nine active frames exceeds 10%. A complete export with zero live rows also fails the draft's header-only rule. A fresh export can hit the same limits. Decide whether a signed zero-row export is valid evidence and how operators resolve a legitimate withdrawal the automatic limits block. A proposed recovery is a separate, authorized review of exact candidate IDs and current versions, with a new atomic apply. This recovery is an open decision.

A guard failure should show the eligible retirement count, pre-apply active count, and limit. A pending move should show frame ID, origin, destination, and what clears it if the destination export never arrives or is rejected. Use frame-level diagnostics for absent frames and job-level diagnostics for guards. The current row-error table requires a positive CSV row number. [Existing diagnostic schema](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/src/backend/src/main/resources/db/migration/V3__create_inventory_import.sql:30)

### 5. Major — Make the signed evidence and validation rules precise

Specify a versioned signed format, UTC timestamp encoding, canonical scope identifiers, producer authorization for each scope, and manifest byte and event-count limits. Capture the CSV rows, expected count, and lifecycle facts consistently. A real producer needs stable frame identities across regions and a reliable lifecycle history before retirement is enabled.

Extract scope evidence independently of other validation. The current parser can stop at an invalid status before checking an invalid region. Count each malformed logical record once, and define duplicate-ID and malformed-present-plus-withdrawal behavior explicitly. [Current CSV parser](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/src/backend/src/main/java/com/global/ct/frameinventory/inventoryimport/InventoryCsvReader.java:103)

## Alternatives weighed

- An upstream API or a second authoritative ID list can establish completeness. The signed manifest keeps the existing operator upload flow and lets the producer bind lifecycle evidence to that exact export.
- Retiring at the origin and reactivating at the destination would temporarily hide a valid frame. Waiting for an entire regional batch makes one late region delay the others. Signed move evidence allows independent regional imports.
- Automatic reinstatement based on row presence would make a stray row enough to restore a frame. A signed event provides a dated source decision and supports an unchanged returning row.
- Batched retirement would shorten individual lock holds at the cost of partial commits. The agreed single transaction keeps inventory, the job outcome, and the watermark together.

## Key decisions and staging for next steps

1. Settle per-frame event ordering, scope authority, and precedence over manual changes. Write a lifecycle decision table for move, withdraw, and reinstate.
2. Write an admission and replay table, including committed replay after expiry, a same-time conflict, and an expired or failed uncommitted attempt.
3. Decide how to handle signed empty exports and legitimate above-limit withdrawals. Define what the operator sees and how a blocked change can be resolved.
4. In GLO-33, implement compatible reads and write-path guards before enabling retirement. Verify both move arrival orders, stale broad snapshots, manual changes between staging and apply, manifest tampering, guard boundaries, apply rollback, and lost commit responses. Assert job results, frame history, and watermarks together. Benchmark the full 10,000-row workload under contention before rollout.

from pathlib import Path

path = Path('/private/tmp/glo-34-goldfish.8B6Agx/concepts_brief.md')
brief = path.read_text()
brief = brief.replace('Reviewed working contract. Open decisions are identified below.', 'Reviewed working contract with follow-up decisions incorporated.')
brief = brief.replace('[Contract reviewed]', '[Original contract reviewed]')
start = brief.index('| Freshness |')
end = brief.index('\\n\\n## Analysis', start)
brief = brief[:start] + '''| Freshness and replay | Return the original result for an authorized exact committed replay, including after expiry. Compare the signed manifest contents and CSV checksum with the committed record. Reject future captures and new apply attempts older than 24 hours. Check age at manifest verification and again before apply. |
| Same-scope ordering | Reject different signed contents at the same capture time and identify the earlier committed job. A correction needs a fresh capture. |
| Overlapping scopes | Reject a narrower snapshot older than a committed ancestor. An older broad snapshot skips every write touching a newer descendant through the frame's current or proposed scope. Reject incoming snapshots that overlap a committed snapshot in a different scope at the same capture time. Report the conflicting scope, capture time, and job ID. |
| Scope and malformed data | Reject out-of-scope rows, an unverifiable required scope field, a missing recoverable frame ID, and unrecoverable parse errors. An identifiable malformed row with verified scope counts as present. More than 5% malformed logical data records fails the job. A valid header and verified signed row count of zero follow normal snapshot rules. |
| Lifecycle order | The source assigns one increasing sequence per frame across regions. Each signed event includes a stable event ID and effective UTC time. Skip older events and reject different events claiming the same sequence. Repeated applied events make no additional changes. |
| Moves | Origin evidence keeps the frame active and reports the pending destination. Seeing the event at the origin does not mark it applied. A destination export with the same event and a valid destination row can apply the move. Both arrival orders must leave the frame active at the destination with no intermediate retirement. |
| Manual precedence | Compare the event's effective time with the app's recorded time for the latest manual edit or deletion, including deletion history when no current version exists. The manual action wins if it occurred at or after the source event. Report the skip and preserve the last applied source sequence. |
| Withdrawal | Require a signed withdrawal effective by capture time. Protect newer edits or moves. Reject a live row paired with a withdrawal for the same frame. Keep unexplained absences active and report them in diagnostics. |
| Reinstatement | Require a signed reinstatement effective after the withdrawal and by capture time, plus a valid row in the destination. Matching the old frame details is allowed. |
| Retired frames | Append a RETIRED version with withdrawal and job lineage. Expose it through direct lookup, history and an explicit retired filter. Ordinary edit and delete actions reject it. Only a signed reinstatement can reopen it. The existing force rule for manual deletion remains separate. |
| Apply limits | Use one transaction. Retire at most the lesser of 100 frames or 10% of pre-apply active frames in scope. Active means a current LIVE, PENDING, MAINTENANCE, BLOCKED, or DRAFT version. Wait at most 1 second for the exclusive inventory lock and allow 5 seconds for the whole apply once acquired. Benchmark a 10,000-row import with competing writes. |
| Guard recovery | Fail above-cap jobs atomically. List blocked frame IDs, signed withdrawals, eligible retirement counts and the cap. Single-frame approval follows with deployed authorization. It will require an explicit permission, a current-version and evidence recheck, and an audit record. |''' + brief[end:]
start = brief.index('### 1. Blocker')
end = brief.index('\\n## Alternatives weighed', start)
brief = brief[:start] + '''### 1. Open decision — Protect a move while the destination is pending

The latest verified source event and the last applied source event can differ. If move 12 is confirmed by Region A but is waiting for Region B, relying on the last applied sequence alone can admit withdrawal 11 from a delayed export. Decide what evidence must be recorded when an origin reports a move and how it blocks older events while allowing the matching destination to apply.
